I am sorry, but you do not know what a RESTful API is. I know you are a seasoned developer who has integrated APIs of all kinds, and you may even have dozens in production across multiple languages. But all of that only proves you have followed the industry's good practices and read immeasurable lines of documentation, which is good. However, none of it certifies your knowledge of RESTful. Don't panic! You are not alone. Most developers I know could not define it, implement it or point out its strengths either. That is why in this article I am going to explain its virtues with examples that are easy to understand. And you may well never look at an API the same way again once you finish reading. You have been warned!

API RESTful is often used as a synonym for REST API (Representational State Transfer), and the nuance matters. REST is not an HTTP interface: it is an architectural style, defined by Roy Fielding in his doctoral dissertation (2000), that imposes constraints:

  • Client-server architecture: The client and the server must be separated.
  • Stateless: Each client request to the server must contain all the information needed to understand and process the request. In other words, the server will not keep information about the client's state between requests.
  • Cacheable: Responses must be explicitly marked as cacheable or non-cacheable.
  • Layered system: The architecture can be composed of layers, where each layer has a specific function and they are isolated from each other.
  • Uniform interface: Communication between the client and the server must be predictable, with a well-defined pattern.
  • Code on demand (optional): The server can send executable code to the client, such as JavaScript scripts, to extend the client's functionality.

In other words, REST is a set of architectural principles for serving resources, usually over HTTP. It is so ingrained in web development, and so standardized, that it feels strange when we do not see it.

And here comes the uncomfortable part: strictly speaking, REST already includes everything you are about to read in this article. Hypermedia is part of the uniform interface constraint, and "RESTful" is simply the adjective, "conforming to REST". What has happened is that popular usage has been degrading "REST" until it means "HTTP API that returns JSON", so much so that Fielding himself published a famous article in 2008, REST APIs must be hypertext-driven, complaining that we call REST any RPC dressed up in HTTP. The Richardson Maturity Model put numbers on that distance: level 0, a single RPC-style endpoint; level 1, resources with their own URI; level 2, HTTP verbs and status codes used properly; level 3, hypermedia. The vast majority of the "REST" APIs you consume every day stay at level 2.

In this article I will use RESTful to refer to that level 3, the one Fielding demands. The goal is to turn an API into a predictable, standardized and self-descriptive interface. With just the base URL, the client will be able to explore every resource, without resorting to external documentation. In addition, we will have the flexibility to change routes without affecting the client, or even play with several communication protocols.

But first there is a concept you must know: HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State). This concept is fundamental to understanding how a RESTful API can be self-descriptive and navigable.

HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State)

Hypermedia is one of the key characteristics of RESTful: it allows clients to dynamically discover resources through links provided in the responses. They usually live under the _links parent.

{
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "update": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "PUT"
        },
        "delete": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "DELETE"
        },
        "friends": {
            "href": "/users/123/friends",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "posts": {
            "href": "/users/123/posts",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "search": {
            "href": "/search/?query={query}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        }
    }
}

Thanks to this, clients can navigate the API by parsing and following the links to reach the information they need, similar to how you would browse the internet. Furthermore, since you jump between relative routes (href) using their names as identifiers (the object key), the backend could change the addresses without affecting the client. It is very powerful because the client is not tied to a fixed route structure; it moves between nodes.

Notice the use of templated: true in the last link. It indicates that the href contains a URI template (following RFC 6570) that must be filled in with specific values before use. It is an elegant way to discover parameterized endpoints. For example, the client could replace {query} with "restful api" to search for related content.

An honest note before we continue: the _links convention comes from HAL (Hypertext Application Language), but HAL does not define the method field; its links only contemplate properties such as href, templated, type or title. I add it because in practice it helps the API be self-descriptive, and it is a common extension. If you need actions with formalized methods and fields, look at Siren; if you prefer pure HAL, omit method and trust the protocol's conventions (rule 2).

Not every resource needs hypermedia, only the relevant ones with the right context. For example, it would make no sense to include links to a shopping cart in a blog article, but it would be interesting for an article to include the link to the author, the comments or related articles.

Now that we understand the importance of HATEOAS, let's look at the rules a RESTful API must follow.

The 6 rules of a RESTful API

I am not making these rules up: they are the six conditions Fielding lists in the article I mentioned earlier, adapted here with examples.

1. Don't depend on a single protocol

Use resource identifiers (URIs) to define resources. In other words, instead of using a URL (http://example.com/api/users/123), use a URI that indicates its location and ignores the protocol (/users/123). This way you could use others such as WebSocket, MQTT, NNTP, RPC, etc. Of course you can use HTTP, but you must not depend only on it. For example, if your API is designed to work exclusively over HTTP, it would not be strictly RESTful.

2. Don't change the protocol

Don't reinvent the wheel. Don't get creative with protocols. For example, if you use HTTP, follow the conventions: GET to fetch resources, POST to create, PUT to replace, PATCH for partial updates and DELETE to remove. Use the proper HTTP response statuses: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, etc. Using MQTT? Use the proper commands and statuses.

3. Focus on media types, not URIs

Instead of documenting each URI externally, you must make your API describe the media types it handles. It is the most misunderstood rule of the six, and for Fielding it is where almost all the descriptive effort should go. The idea: instead of publishing a list of routes (what we usually call "the documentation"), you define and document your media types (for example application/vnd.myshop.product+json), that is, what the fields of each representation mean and how its links are processed. The client decides what to do based on the Content-Type it receives, not on the URI it called. URIs become interchangeable details.

For example, the resource for a user with little information could be:

{
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "_links": {
        "self": "/users/123",
        "friends": "/users/123/friends",
        "lastInvoice": "/users/123/invoice/last"
    }
}

While the resource for a user with more information could be:

{
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "GET",
            "type": "application/json"
        },
        "friends": {
            "href": "/users/123/friends",
            "method": "GET",
            "type": "text/csv"
        },
        "lastInvoice": {
            "href": "/users/123/invoice/last",
            "method": "GET",
            "type": "application/pdf"
        }
    }
}

4. Don't assume URI structures

You must not store or reuse URI structures in the client. An API could change them without notice, and your client would obviously stop working. Instead, parse the links and follow the relative identifiers (rel).

A resource can have the following structure:

{
    "id": 987,
    "name": "Totoro plush",
    "price": 19.99,
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/products/987",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "addToCart": {
            "href": "/cart/add/987",
            "method": "POST"
        },
        "reviews": {
            "href": "/products/987/reviews",
            "method": "GET"
        }
    }
}

And the next day:

{
    "id": 987,
    "name": "Totoro plush",
    "price": 19.99,
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/shop/item/987",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "addToCart": {
            "href": "/shop/cart/987",
            "method": "POST"
        },
        "reviews": {
            "href": "/shop/item/987/reviews",
            "method": "GET"
        }
    }
}

5. Avoid resource "types"

Don't expose the hierarchy, permissions or types of resources in the API. The client neither cares nor should know. For example, you should not have a /users/admin/123 or /users/guest/123 resource. Instead, use the links to define the actions that can be performed on the resource.

6. Start with a bookmark (root resource) and let the client explore

Clients must start with a root URL (or bookmark), and from there they will navigate your API-verse.

{
    "message": "Welcome to my RESTful API",
    "_links": {
        "users": {
            "href": "/users",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "products": {
            "href": "/products",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "orders": {
            "href": "/orders",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "search": {
            "href": "/search/?query={query}&page={page}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        },
        "user-by-id": {
            "href": "/users/{user_id}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        },
        "product-search": {
            "href": "/products/search/?name={name}&category={category}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        }
    }
}

Notice that several links use templated: true, the URI templates we saw in the HATEOAS section: the client discovers even the parameterized endpoints without leaving the response.

You now have a general idea of how to build a RESTful API. Between the REST principles, the RESTful API rules and the HATEOAS concept, you will be able to build a solid API.

FAQ

How do I indicate the version of the API or endpoint?

The most common approach is to include the version in the URL, for example: /api/v1/users. However, if you want to follow the RESTful rules, you should take the version out of the URI. The most recommended option is to negotiate it with the Accept header using the structure application/vnd.example.v1+json, where example is the name of your API and v1 is the version.

For example, my API is called dream and the latest version is 2.1, so the header would be: Accept: application/vnd.dream.v2.1+json.

Another simpler option, although less recommended, is to use a custom header such as Api-Version, where the value would be 2.1. That said, avoid the classic X- prefix (X-API-Version): it has been discouraged since 2012 by RFC 6648.

How do I handle pagination?

You will need to include metadata in the response to indicate the pagination with meta.

A pagination example could be:

{
    "data": [...],
    "meta": {
        "total": 150,
        "page": 1,
        "perPage": 10,
        "hasNext": true,
        "hasPrevious": false
    },
    "_links": {
        "self": {"href": "/api/items?page=1", "method": "GET"},
        "next": {"href": "/api/items?page=2", "method": "GET"},
        "first": {"href": "/api/items?page=1", "method": "GET"},
        "last": {"href": "/api/items?page=15", "method": "GET"}
    }
}

Where:

  • total: Total number of available items. Not on the current page, but in the whole collection.
  • page: Current page number. It can never be 0 or negative.
  • perPage: Number of items per page.
  • hasNext: Indicates whether there are more pages available.
  • hasPrevious: Indicates whether there are previous pages available.
  • _links: Links to navigate the pagination, such as next, previous, first, last and self. When a link does not apply (there is no previous page on the first page), it is omitted, not set to null: that is how HAL does it and it avoids ambiguity for the client.

You can also use templates to let the client specify the page number:

{
    "_links": {
        "page": {
            "href": "/api/items?page={page}&perPage={perPage}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        }
    }
}

How do I handle errors?

Here there is a standard, although few people know it: RFC 9457 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs, which updates RFC 7807 from 2016). It defines the application/problem+json media type with five fields: type (a URI identifying the problem category), title (a short, stable summary), status (the HTTP status code), detail (an explanation of this specific occurrence) and instance (the URI of the affected resource). And it allows you to add your own extension fields.

For example, a response with a 404 Not Found status and the Content-Type: application/problem+json header would carry this body:

{
    "type": "https://example.com/errors/article-not-found",
    "title": "Article not found",
    "status": 404,
    "detail": "There is no article with id c9bb4e4a",
    "instance": "/api/blog/c9bb4e4a"
}

If you are starting an API from scratch, my advice is to use Problem Details: it is the standard and your clients will thank you. In my projects I use my own convention (type, errors, data and meta) that integrates with the response structure of my use cases; if you are curious, I explain it in Implementing Clean Architecture in Python.

Conclusions

A true RESTful API, the one Fielding described, is not an evolution of REST: it is complete REST, the level 3 of the Richardson Maturity Model that almost nobody reaches. While popular usage stops at resources, verbs and status codes, hypermedia adds what turns an API into a self-descriptive and navigable interface.

For errors you already have a standard, RFC 9457: use it and your clients will always know what to expect.

In short, a well-implemented RESTful API does not just transfer data; it takes the client by the hand through all of its resources, creating an experience that is intuitive and resilient to change. Which is essential for a long-term project.

Sources

If you want to keep digging into the topic, here are some recommended sources:

  • Roy Fielding's Dissertation
  • REST APIs must be hypertext-driven by Roy Fielding.
  • Richardson Maturity Model by Martin Fowler.
  • RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
  • HAL - Hypertext Application Language
  • REST Architectural Constraints by Lokesh Gupta.

It would also be interesting to read more about HAL and JSON-LD, since they are formats that make it easier to implement HATEOAS and the self-description of RESTful APIs.

sentences.en: But all of that only proves you have followed the industry's good practices and read immeasurable lines of documentation, which is good.

sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在本文中我将通过易于理解的示例来解释它的优点。

sentences.en: And you may well never look at an API the same way again once you finish reading.

blocks.html_en: API RESTful is often used as a synonym for REST API (Representational State Transfer), and the nuance matters. REST is not an HTTP interface: it is an architectural style, defined by Roy Fielding in his doctoral dissertation (2000), that imposes constraints:

sentences.en: API RESTful is often used as a synonym for REST API (Representational State Transfer), and the nuance matters.
sentences.zh: RESTful API 通常被用作 REST API（表述性状态传输）的同义词，其中的细微差别很重要。

sentences.en: REST is not an HTTP interface: it is an architectural style, defined by Roy Fielding in his doctoral dissertation (2000), that imposes constraints:
sentences.zh: REST 不是 HTTP 接口：它是一种架构风格，由 Roy Fielding 在他的博士论文（2000 年）中定义，它施加了约束：

blocks.html_en: • Client-server architecture: The client and the server must be separated.

sentences.en: Client-server architecture: The client and the server must be separated.
sentences.zh: 客户端-服务器架构：客户端和服务器必须分开。

blocks.html_en: • Stateless: Each client request to the server must contain all the information needed to understand and process the request. In other words, the server will not keep information about the client's state between requests.

sentences.en: Stateless: Each client request to the server must contain all the information needed to understand and process the request.
sentences.zh: 无状态：每个客户端向服务器发出的请求都必须包含理解和处理该请求所需的所有信息。

sentences.en: In other words, the server will not keep information about the client's state between requests.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，服务器不会在请求之间保留有关客户端状态的信息。

blocks.html_en: • Cacheable: Responses must be explicitly marked as cacheable or non-cacheable.

sentences.en: Cacheable: Responses must be explicitly marked as cacheable or non-cacheable.
sentences.zh: 可缓存：响应必须显式标记为可缓存或不可缓存。

blocks.html_en: • Layered system: The architecture can be composed of layers, where each layer has a specific function and they are isolated from each other.

sentences.en: Layered system: The architecture can be composed of layers, where each layer has a specific function and they are isolated from each other.
sentences.zh: 分层系统：体系结构可以由层组成，每个层都有特定的功能，并且它们之间相互隔离。

blocks.html_en: • Uniform interface: Communication between the client and the server must be predictable, with a well-defined pattern.

sentences.en: Uniform interface: Communication between the client and the server must be predictable, with a well-defined pattern.
sentences.zh: 统一接口：客户端和服务器之间的通信必须是可预测的，具有明确定义的模式。

blocks.html_en: • Code on demand (optional): The server can send executable code to the client, such as JavaScript scripts, to extend the client's functionality.

sentences.en: Code on demand (optional): The server can send executable code to the client, such as JavaScript scripts, to extend the client's functionality.
sentences.zh: 按需代码（可选）：服务器可以向客户端发送可执行代码，例如 JavaScript 脚本，以扩展客户端的功能。

blocks.html_en: In other words, REST is a set of architectural principles for serving resources, usually over HTTP. It is so ingrained in web development, and so standardized, that it feels strange when we do not see it.

sentences.en: In other words, REST is a set of architectural principles for serving resources, usually over HTTP.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，REST 是一组通常通过 HTTP 提供资源服务的架构原则。

sentences.en: It is so ingrained in web development, and so standardized, that it feels strange when we do not see it.
sentences.zh: 它在 Web 开发中如此根深蒂固，并且如此标准化，以至于当我们看不到它时会感觉很奇怪。

blocks.html_en: And here comes the uncomfortable part: strictly speaking, REST already includes everything you are about to read in this article. Hypermedia is part of the uniform interface constraint, and "RESTful" is simply the adjective, "conforming to REST". What has happened is that popular usage has been degrading "REST" until it means "HTTP API that returns JSON", so much so that Fielding himself published a famous article in 2008, REST APIs must be hypertext-driven, complaining that we call REST any RPC dressed up in HTTP. The Richardson Maturity Model put numbers on that distance: level 0, a single RPC-style endpoint; level 1, resources with their own URI; level 2, HTTP verbs and status codes used properly; level 3, hypermedia. The vast majority of the "REST" APIs you consume every day stay at level 2.

sentences.en: And here comes the uncomfortable part: strictly speaking, REST already includes everything you are about to read in this article.
sentences.zh: 令人不舒服的部分来了：严格来说，REST 已经包含了您将在本文中阅读的所有内容。

sentences.en: Hypermedia is part of the uniform interface constraint, and "RESTful" is simply the adjective, "conforming to REST".
sentences.zh: 超媒体是统一接口约束的一部分，“RESTful”只是形容词，“符合 REST”。

sentences.en: What has happened is that popular usage has been degrading "REST" until it means "HTTP API that returns JSON", so much so that Fielding himself published a famous article in 2008, REST APIs must be hypertext-driven, complaining that we call REST any RPC dressed up in HTTP.
sentences.zh: 所发生的情况是，流行的用法一直在贬低“REST”，直到它意味着“返回 JSON 的 HTTP API”，以至于 Fielding 本人在 2008 年发表了一篇著名的文章，REST API 必须是超文本驱动的，抱怨我们将任何披着 HTTP 外衣的 RPC 称为 REST。

sentences.en: The Richardson Maturity Model put numbers on that distance: level 0, a single RPC-style endpoint; level 1, resources with their own URI; level 2, HTTP verbs and status codes used properly; level 3, hypermedia.
sentences.zh: Richardson 成熟度模型对这个距离给出了数字：0 级，单个 RPC 风格的端点； level 1，资源有自己的URI； 2级，正确使用HTTP动词和状态码；第三级，超媒体。

sentences.en: The vast majority of the "REST" APIs you consume every day stay at level 2.
sentences.zh: 您每天使用的绝大多数“REST”API 都处于 2 级。

blocks.html_en: In this article I will use RESTful to refer to that level 3, the one Fielding demands. The goal is to turn an API into a predictable, standardized and self-descriptive interface. With just the base URL, the client will be able to explore every resource, without resorting to external documentation. In addition, we will have the flexibility to change routes without affecting the client, or even play with several communication protocols.

sentences.en: In this article I will use RESTful to refer to that level 3, the one Fielding demands.
sentences.zh: 在本文中，我将使用 RESTful 来指代 Fielding 所要求的第 3 级。

sentences.en: The goal is to turn an API into a predictable, standardized and self-descriptive interface.
sentences.zh: 目标是将 API 转变为可预测、标准化和自描述的接口。

sentences.en: With just the base URL, the client will be able to explore every resource, without resorting to external documentation.
sentences.zh: 只需基本 URL，客户端就能够探索每个资源，而无需求助于外部文档。

sentences.en: In addition, we will have the flexibility to change routes without affecting the client, or even play with several communication protocols.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们将可以灵活地更改路由而不影响客户端，甚至可以使用多种通信协议。

blocks.html_en: But first there is a concept you must know: HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State). This concept is fundamental to understanding how a RESTful API can be self-descriptive and navigable.

sentences.en: But first there is a concept you must know: HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State).
sentences.zh: 但首先有一个概念你必须知道：HATEOAS（超媒体作为应用程序状态引擎）。

sentences.en: This concept is fundamental to understanding how a RESTful API can be self-descriptive and navigable.
sentences.zh: 这个概念对于理解 RESTful API 如何实现自描述和可导航至关重要。

blocks.html_en: HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State)

sentences.en: HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State)
sentences.zh: HATEOAS（超媒体作为应用程序状态引擎）

blocks.html_en: Hypermedia is one of the key characteristics of RESTful: it allows clients to dynamically discover resources through links provided in the responses. They usually live under the _links parent.

sentences.en: Hypermedia is one of the key characteristics of RESTful: it allows clients to dynamically discover resources through links provided in the responses.
sentences.zh: 超媒体是 RESTful 的关键特征之一：它允许客户端通过响应中提供的链接动态发现资源。

sentences.en: They usually live under the _links parent.
sentences.zh: 它们通常位于 _links 父级下。

blocks.html_en: Thanks to this, clients can navigate the API by parsing and following the links to reach the information they need, similar to how you would browse the internet. Furthermore, since you jump between relative routes (href) using their names as identifiers (the object key), the backend could change the addresses without affecting the client. It is very powerful because the client is not tied to a fixed route structure; it moves between nodes.

sentences.en: Thanks to this, clients can navigate the API by parsing and following the links to reach the information they need, similar to how you would browse the internet.
sentences.zh: 因此，客户可以通过解析和跟踪链接来导航 API，以获取他们需要的信息，类似于浏览互联网的方式。

sentences.en: Furthermore, since you jump between relative routes (href) using their names as identifiers (the object key), the backend could change the addresses without affecting the client.
sentences.zh: 此外，由于您使用相对路由（href）的名称作为标识符（对象键）在相对路由（href）之间跳转，因此后端可以更改地址而不影响客户端。

sentences.en: It is very powerful because the client is not tied to a fixed route structure; it moves between nodes.
sentences.zh: 它非常强大，因为客户端不受固定路由结构的束缚；它在节点之间移动。

blocks.html_en: Notice the use of templated: true in the last link. It indicates that the href contains a URI template (following RFC 6570) that must be filled in with specific values before use. It is an elegant way to discover parameterized endpoints. For example, the client could replace {query} with "restful api" to search for related content.

sentences.en: Notice the use of templated: true in the last link.
sentences.zh: 请注意最后一个链接中 templated: true 的使用。

sentences.en: It indicates that the href contains a URI template (following RFC 6570) that must be filled in with specific values before use.
sentences.zh: 它指示 href 包含 URI 模板（遵循 RFC 6570），在使用前必须填写特定值。

sentences.en: It is an elegant way to discover parameterized endpoints.
sentences.zh: 这是发现参数化端点的一种优雅方式。

sentences.en: For example, the client could replace {query} with "restful api" to search for related content.
sentences.zh: 例如，客户端可以将 {query} 替换为“restful api”来搜索相关内容。

blocks.html_en: An honest note before we continue: the _links convention comes from HAL (Hypertext Application Language), but HAL does not define the method field; its links only contemplate properties such as href, templated, type or title. I add it because in practice it helps the API be self-descriptive, and it is a common extension. If you need actions with formalized methods and fields, look at Siren; if you prefer pure HAL, omit method and trust the protocol's conventions (rule 2).

sentences.en: An honest note before we continue: the _links convention comes from HAL (Hypertext Application Language), but HAL does not define the method field; its links only contemplate properties such as href, templated, type or title.
sentences.zh: 在我们继续之前，诚实地说：_links 约定来自 HAL（超文本应用程序语言），但 HAL 没有定义方法字段；它的链接仅考虑诸如 href、模板化、类型或标题之类的属性。

sentences.en: I add it because in practice it helps the API be self-descriptive, and it is a common extension.
sentences.zh: 我添加它是因为在实践中它有助于 API 的自我描述，并且它是一个常见的扩展。

sentences.en: If you need actions with formalized methods and fields, look at Siren; if you prefer pure HAL, omit method and trust the protocol's conventions (rule 2).
sentences.zh: 如果您需要使用形式化方法和字段进行操作，请查看 Siren；如果您更喜欢纯 HAL，请省略方法并信任协议的约定（规则 2）。

blocks.html_en: Not every resource needs hypermedia, only the relevant ones with the right context. For example, it would make no sense to include links to a shopping cart in a blog article, but it would be interesting for an article to include the link to the author, the comments or related articles.

sentences.en: Not every resource needs hypermedia, only the relevant ones with the right context.
sentences.zh: 并非所有资源都需要超媒体，只有具有正确上下文的相关资源才需要。

sentences.en: For example, it would make no sense to include links to a shopping cart in a blog article, but it would be interesting for an article to include the link to the author, the comments or related articles.
sentences.zh: 例如，在博客文章中包含购物车的链接是没有意义的，但文章包含作者、评论或相关文章的链接会很有趣。

blocks.html_en: Now that we understand the importance of HATEOAS, let's look at the rules a RESTful API must follow.

sentences.en: Now that we understand the importance of HATEOAS, let's look at the rules a RESTful API must follow.
sentences.zh: 现在我们了解了 HATEOAS 的重要性，让我们看看 RESTful API 必须遵循的规则。

blocks.html_en: The 6 rules of a RESTful API

sentences.en: The 6 rules of a RESTful API
sentences.zh: RESTful API 的 6 条规则

blocks.html_en: I am not making these rules up: they are the six conditions Fielding lists in the article I mentioned earlier, adapted here with examples.

sentences.en: I am not making these rules up: they are the six conditions Fielding lists in the article I mentioned earlier, adapted here with examples.
sentences.zh: 这些规则不是我制定的：它们是我之前提到的文章中列出的六个条件，此处通过示例进行了调整。

blocks.html_en: 1. Don't depend on a single protocol

sentences.en: Don't depend on a single protocol
sentences.zh: 不依赖于单一协议

blocks.html_en: Use resource identifiers (URIs) to define resources. In other words, instead of using a URL (http://example.com/api/users/123), use a URI that indicates its location and ignores the protocol (/users/123). This way you could use others such as WebSocket, MQTT, NNTP, RPC, etc. Of course you can use HTTP, but you must not depend only on it. For example, if your API is designed to work exclusively over HTTP, it would not be strictly RESTful.

sentences.en: Use resource identifiers (URIs) to define resources.
sentences.zh: 使用资源标识符 (URI) 来定义资源。

sentences.en: In other words, instead of using a URL (http://example.com/api/users/123), use a URI that indicates its location and ignores the protocol (/users/123).
sentences.zh: 换句话说，不要使用 URL (http://example.com/api/users/123)，而是使用指示其位置并忽略协议 (/users/123) 的 URI。

sentences.en: This way you could use others such as WebSocket, MQTT, NNTP, RPC, etc. Of course you can use HTTP, but you must not depend only on it.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以使用其他的如WebSocket、MQTT、NNTP、RPC等。当然你可以使用HTTP，但你不能仅仅依赖它。

sentences.en: For example, if your API is designed to work exclusively over HTTP, it would not be strictly RESTful.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果您的 API 设计为专门通过 HTTP 工作，那么它就不是严格的 RESTful。

blocks.html_en: 2. Don't change the protocol

sentences.en: Don't change the protocol
sentences.zh: 不要改变协议

blocks.html_en: Don't reinvent the wheel. Don't get creative with protocols. For example, if you use HTTP, follow the conventions: GET to fetch resources, POST to create, PUT to replace, PATCH for partial updates and DELETE to remove. Use the proper HTTP response statuses: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, etc. Using MQTT? Use the proper commands and statuses.

sentences.en: Don't reinvent the wheel.
sentences.zh: 不要重新发明轮子。

sentences.en: Don't get creative with protocols.
sentences.zh: 不要对协议发挥创意。

sentences.en: For example, if you use HTTP, follow the conventions: GET to fetch resources, POST to create, PUT to replace, PATCH for partial updates and DELETE to remove.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果您使用 HTTP，请遵循以下约定：GET 获取资源、POST 进行创建、PUT 进行替换、PATCH 进行部分更新以及 DELETE 进行删除。

sentences.en: Use the proper HTTP response statuses: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, etc. Using MQTT?
sentences.zh: 使用正确的 HTTP 响应状态：200 OK、201 Created、204 No Content、400 Bad Request、404 Not Found 等。使用 MQTT？

sentences.en: Use the proper commands and statuses.
sentences.zh: 使用正确的命令和状态。

blocks.html_en: 3. Focus on media types, not URIs

sentences.en: Focus on media types, not URIs
sentences.zh: 关注媒体类型，而不是 URI

blocks.html_en: Instead of documenting each URI externally, you must make your API describe the media types it handles. It is the most misunderstood rule of the six, and for Fielding it is where almost all the descriptive effort should go. The idea: instead of publishing a list of routes (what we usually call "the documentation"), you define and document your media types (for example application/vnd.myshop.product+json), that is, what the fields of each representation mean and how its links are processed. The client decides what to do based on the Content-Type it receives, not on the URI it called. URIs become interchangeable details.

sentences.en: Instead of documenting each URI externally, you must make your API describe the media types it handles.
sentences.zh: 您必须让 API 描述它处理的媒体类型，而不是在外部记录每个 URI。

sentences.en: It is the most misunderstood rule of the six, and for Fielding it is where almost all the descriptive effort should go.
sentences.zh: 这是六条规则中最容易被误解的一条，对菲尔丁来说，几乎所有的描述工作都应该放在这条规则上。

sentences.en: The idea: instead of publishing a list of routes (what we usually call "the documentation"), you define and document your media types (for example application/vnd.myshop.product+json), that is, what the fields of each representation mean and how its links are processed.
sentences.zh: 想法：您不用发布路由列表（我们通常称之为“文档”），而是定义并记录您的媒体类型（例如 application/vnd.myshop.product+json），即每个表示的字段含义以及其链接的处理方式。

sentences.en: The client decides what to do based on the Content-Type it receives, not on the URI it called.
sentences.zh: 客户端根据它收到的 Content-Type 决定要做什么，而不是根据它调用的 URI。

sentences.en: URIs become interchangeable details.
sentences.zh: URI 成为可互换的详细信息。

blocks.html_en: FAQ
How do I indicate the version of the API or endpoint?

sentences.en: How do I indicate the version of the API or endpoint?

content_html_zh:
抱歉，您不知道什么是 RESTful API。 我知道您是一位经验丰富的开发人员，集成了各种 API，您甚至可能有数十个跨多种语言的生产环境。 但所有这些只能证明您遵循了行业的良好实践并阅读了无数的文档，这很好。 然而，这些都不能证明您对 RESTful 的了解。 不要恐慌！ 你并不孤单。 我认识的大多数开发人员都无法定义它、实现它或指出它的优势。 这就是为什么在本文中我将通过易于理解的示例来解释它的优点。 一旦你读完，你可能再也不会以同样的方式看待 API。 您已被警告！

RESTful API 通常被用作 REST API（表述性状态传输）的同义词，其中的细微差别很重要。 REST 不是 HTTP 接口：它是一种架构风格，由 Roy Fielding 在他的博士论文（2000 年）中定义，它施加了约束：

  • 客户端-服务器架构：客户端和服务器必须分开。
  • 无状态：每个客户端向服务器发出的请求都必须包含理解和处理该请求所需的所有信息。 换句话说，服务器不会在请求之间保留有关客户端状态的信息。
  • 可缓存：响应必须显式标记为可缓存或不可缓存。
  • 分层系统：体系结构可以由层组成，每个层都有特定的功能，并且它们之间相互隔离。
  • 统一接口：客户端和服务器之间的通信必须是可预测的，具有明确定义的模式。
  • 按需代码（可选）：服务器可以向客户端发送可执行代码，例如 JavaScript 脚本，以扩展客户端的功能。

换句话说，REST 是一组通常通过 HTTP 提供资源服务的架构原则。 它在 Web 开发中如此根深蒂固，并且如此标准化，以至于当我们看不到它时会感觉很奇怪。

令人不舒服的部分来了：严格来说，REST 已经包含了您将在本文中阅读的所有内容。 超媒体是统一接口约束的一部分，“RESTful”只是形容词，“符合 REST”。 所发生的情况是，流行的用法一直在贬低“REST”，直到它意味着“返回 JSON 的 HTTP API”，以至于 Fielding 本人在 2008 年发表了一篇著名的文章，REST API 必须是超文本驱动的，抱怨我们将任何披着 HTTP 外衣的 RPC 称为 REST。 Richardson 成熟度模型对这个距离给出了数字：0 级，单个 RPC 风格的端点； level 1，资源有自己的URI； 2级，正确使用HTTP动词和状态码；第三级，超媒体。 您每天使用的绝大多数“REST”API 都处于 2 级。

在本文中，我将使用 RESTful 来指代 Fielding 所要求的第 3 级。 目标是将 API 转变为可预测、标准化和自描述的接口。 只需基本 URL，客户端就能够探索每个资源，而无需求助于外部文档。 此外，我们将可以灵活地更改路由而不影响客户端，甚至可以使用多种通信协议。

但首先有一个概念你必须知道：HATEOAS（超媒体作为应用程序状态引擎）。 这个概念对于理解 RESTful API 如何实现自描述和可导航至关重要。

HATEOAS（超媒体作为应用程序状态引擎）

超媒体是 RESTful 的关键特征之一：它允许客户端通过响应中提供的链接动态发现资源。 它们通常位于 _links 父级下。

{
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "update": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "PUT"
        },
        "delete": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "DELETE"
        },
        "friends": {
            "href": "/users/123/friends",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "posts": {
            "href": "/users/123/posts",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "search": {
            "href": "/search/?query={query}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        }
    }
}

因此，客户可以通过解析和跟踪链接来导航 API，以获取他们需要的信息，类似于浏览互联网的方式。 此外，由于您使用相对路由（href）的名称作为标识符（对象键）在相对路由（href）之间跳转，因此后端可以更改地址而不影响客户端。 它非常强大，因为客户端不受固定路由结构的束缚；它在节点之间移动。

请注意最后一个链接中 templated: true 的使用。 它指示 href 包含 URI 模板（遵循 RFC 6570），在使用前必须填写特定值。 这是发现参数化端点的一种优雅方式。 例如，客户端可以将 {query} 替换为“restful api”来搜索相关内容。

在我们继续之前，诚实地说：_links 约定来自 HAL（超文本应用程序语言），但 HAL 没有定义方法字段；它的链接仅考虑诸如 href、模板化、类型或标题之类的属性。 我添加它是因为在实践中它有助于 API 的自我描述，并且它是一个常见的扩展。 如果您需要使用形式化方法和字段进行操作，请查看 Siren；如果您更喜欢纯 HAL，请省略方法并信任协议的约定（规则 2）。

并非所有资源都需要超媒体，只有具有正确上下文的相关资源才需要。 例如，在博客文章中包含购物车的链接是没有意义的，但文章包含作者、评论或相关文章的链接会很有趣。

现在我们了解了 HATEOAS 的重要性，让我们看看 RESTful API 必须遵循的规则。

RESTful API 的 6 条规则

这些规则不是我制定的：它们是我之前提到的文章中列出的六个条件，此处通过示例进行了调整。

1. 不依赖于单一协议

使用资源标识符 (URI) 来定义资源。 换句话说，不要使用 URL (http://example.com/api/users/123)，而是使用指示其位置并忽略协议 (/users/123) 的 URI。 这样你就可以使用其他的如WebSocket、MQTT、NNTP、RPC等。当然你可以使用HTTP，但你不能仅仅依赖它。 例如，如果您的 API 设计为专门通过 HTTP 工作，那么它就不是严格的 RESTful。

2. 不要改变协议

不要重新发明轮子。 不要对协议发挥创意。 例如，如果您使用 HTTP，请遵循以下约定：GET 获取资源、POST 进行创建、PUT 进行替换、PATCH 进行部分更新以及 DELETE 进行删除。 使用正确的 HTTP 响应状态：200 OK、201 Created、204 No Content、400 Bad Request、404 Not Found 等。使用 MQTT？ 使用正确的命令和状态。

3. 关注媒体类型，而不是 URI

您必须让 API 描述它处理的媒体类型，而不是在外部记录每个 URI。 这是六条规则中最容易被误解的一条，对菲尔丁来说，几乎所有的描述工作都应该放在这条规则上。 想法：您不用发布路由列表（我们通常称之为“文档”），而是定义并记录您的媒体类型（例如 application/vnd.myshop.product+json），即每个表示的字段含义以及其链接的处理方式。 客户端根据它收到的 Content-Type 决定要做什么，而不是根据它调用的 URI。 URI 成为可互换的详细信息。

例如，信息很少的用户的资源可能是：

{
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "_links": {
        "self": "/users/123",
        "friends": "/users/123/friends",
        "lastInvoice": "/users/123/invoice/last"
    }
}

虽然具有更多信息的用户的资源可以是：

{
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/users/123",
            "method": "GET",
            "type": "application/json"
        },
        "friends": {
            "href": "/users/123/friends",
            "method": "GET",
            "type": "text/csv"
        },
        "lastInvoice": {
            "href": "/users/123/invoice/last",
            "method": "GET",
            "type": "application/pdf"
        }
    }
}

4. 不要假设 URI 结构

您不得在客户端中存储或重复使用 URI 结构。 API 可以在没有通知的情况下更改它们，并且您的客户端显然会停止工作。 相反，解析链接并遵循相对标识符 (rel)。

资源可以具有以下结构：

{
    "id": 987,
    "name": "Totoro plush",
    "price": 19.99,
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/products/987",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "addToCart": {
            "href": "/cart/add/987",
            "method": "POST"
        },
        "reviews": {
            "href": "/products/987/reviews",
            "method": "GET"
        }
    }
}

第二天：

{
    "id": 987,
    "name": "Totoro plush",
    "price": 19.99,
    "_links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "/shop/item/987",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "addToCart": {
            "href": "/shop/cart/987",
            "method": "POST"
        },
        "reviews": {
            "href": "/shop/item/987/reviews",
            "method": "GET"
        }
    }
}

5. 避免资源“类型”

不要在 API 中公开资源的层次结构、权限或类型。 客户既不关心也不应该知道。 例如，您不应拥有 /users/admin/123 或 /users/guest/123 资源。 相反，请使用链接来定义可以对资源执行的操作。

6. 从书签（根资源）开始，让客户探索

客户端必须从根 URL（或书签）开始，然后他们将从那里导航您的 API 领域。

{
    "message": "Welcome to my RESTful API",
    "_links": {
        "users": {
            "href": "/users",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "products": {
            "href": "/products",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "orders": {
            "href": "/orders",
            "method": "GET"
        },
        "search": {
            "href": "/search/?query={query}&page={page}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        },
        "user-by-id": {
            "href": "/users/{user_id}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        },
        "product-search": {
            "href": "/products/search/?name={name}&category={category}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        }
    }
}

请注意，有几个链接使用 templated: true，即我们在 HATEOAS 部分中看到的 URI 模板：客户端甚至可以发现参数化端点，而无需留下响应。

您现在已经大致了解如何构建 RESTful API。 在 REST 原则、RESTful API 规则和 HATEOAS 概念之间，您将能够构建可靠的 API。

FAQ

如何指示 API 或端点的版本？

最常见的方法是在 URL 中包含版本，例如：/api/v1/users。 但是，如果您想遵循 RESTful 规则，则应该从 URI 中取出版本。 最推荐的选项是使用结构 application/vnd.example.v1+json 与 Accept 标头进行协商，其中 example 是 API 的名称，v1 是版本。

例如，我的API名为dream，最新版本是2.1，因此标头为：Accept: application/vnd.dream.v2.1+json。

另一个更简单的选项（尽管不太推荐）是使用自定义标头，例如 Api-Version，其中值是 2.1。 也就是说，请避免使用经典的 X- 前缀 (X-API-Version)：自 2012 年以来，RFC 6648 就不鼓励使用它。

我如何处理分页？

您需要在响应中包含元数据以指示元数据的分页。

分页示例可以是：

{
    "data": [...],
    "meta": {
        "total": 150,
        "page": 1,
        "perPage": 10,
        "hasNext": true,
        "hasPrevious": false
    },
    "_links": {
        "self": {"href": "/api/items?page=1", "method": "GET"},
        "next": {"href": "/api/items?page=2", "method": "GET"},
        "first": {"href": "/api/items?page=1", "method": "GET"},
        "last": {"href": "/api/items?page=15", "method": "GET"}
    }
}

Where:

  • 总计：可用项目总数。 不是在当前页面上，而是在整个集合中。
  • 页码：当前页码。 它永远不可能是 0 或负数。
  • perPage：每页的项目数。
  • hasNext：指示是否还有更多页面可用。
  • hasPrevious：指示是否有前一页可用。
  • _links：用于导航分页的链接，例如下一个、上一个、第一个、最后一个和自身。 当链接不适用时（第一页上没有上一页），它会被省略，而不是设置为 null：这就是 HAL 的做法，它避免了客户端的歧义。

您还可以使用模板让客户端指定页码：

{
    "_links": {
        "page": {
            "href": "/api/items?page={page}&perPage={perPage}",
            "method": "GET",
            "templated": true
        }
    }
}

我如何处理错误？

这里有一个标准，尽管很少有人知道：RFC 9457（HTTP API 的问题详细信息，从 2016 年更新了 RFC 7807）。 它定义了具有五个字段的 application/problem+json 媒体类型：类型（标识问题类别的 URI）、标题（简短、稳定的摘要）、状态（HTTP 状态代码）、详细信息（对此特定事件的解释）和实例（受影响资源的 URI）。 它允许您添加自己的扩展字段。

例如，具有 404 Not Found 状态和 Content-Type: application/problem+json 标头的响应将携带以下正文：

{
    "type": "https://example.com/errors/article-not-found",
    "title": "Article not found",
    "status": 404,
    "detail": "There is no article with id c9bb4e4a",
    "instance": "/api/blog/c9bb4e4a"
}

如果您从头开始创建 API，我的建议是使用问题详细信息：它是标准，您的客户会感谢您。 在我的项目中，我使用自己的约定（类型、错误、数据和元），与我的用例的响应结构集成；如果您好奇，我会在《用 Python 实现干净的架构》中对此进行解释。

结论

Fielding 所描述的真正的 RESTful API 并不是 REST 的演变：它是完整的 REST，即几乎没有人达到的 Richardson 成熟度模型的第 3 级。 虽然流行的用法仅限于资源、动词和状态代码，但超媒体添加了将 API 转变为自描述性和可导航界面的功能。

对于错误，您已经有了一个标准 RFC 9457：使用它，您的客户将始终知道会发生什么。

简而言之，一个实施良好的 RESTful API 不只是传输数据；它还负责传输数据。它带领客户使用其所有资源，创造一种直观且适应变化的体验。 这对于长期项目至关重要。
